en: A moving jeepney keeps moving forward without extra engine force unless friction or brakes stop it due to inertia.
In a vacuum, a heavy bowling ball and a light feather fall at the exact same acceleration rate.
Static friction keeps a parked car from sliding down a hill until the pulling force exceeds its maximum grip.
Magnets attract ferromagnetic metals besides iron, specifically including nickel, cobalt, and steel alloys.
A flashlight bulb only lights up when electrons continuously move through a complete, closed circuit loop.
Sound waves travel much faster through solid materials like steel tracks than through the surrounding air.
Sunlight travels perfectly through the empty vacuum of outer space to reach Earth without needing any physical medium.
Thermal energy always transfers naturally from a hot cup of coffee to the cooler surrounding air.
A ramp makes lifting easier by reducing the required input force, but it increases the distance you must push.
Green mango trees convert light energy from the sun into chemical energy, rather than absorbing energy from soil.
The invisible magnetic field of a bar magnet surrounds the entire object, not just the north and south poles.
A dry cell battery stores chemical energy and converts it into electrical energy only when connected to a circuit.
